chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who has the fasting of two consecutive months upon him, can he break the continuity between the days? He (peace be upon him) said: If he fasts more than a month and connects it, then a matter presents itself to him and he breaks the fast, then there is no problem. But if it is less than a month, or exactly a month, then upon him is that he repeats the fasting.

key_terms.يُفَرِّقُ: To break the continuity / to separate

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one breaks the fast of two consecutive months due to an excuse?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction in expiatory fasting (kaffarah) based on the threshold of completion, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the continuity (ittisal) of the fast. It establishes that once the majority of the period is fulfilled, a valid interruption does not invalidate the obligation, whereas breaking it earlier necessitates a complete restart, highlighting the balance between strict adherence and ease in Shia fiqh.
